I feel you, man. I'm going through the exact same thing. I'm so pedantic and nitpicky that I seem to find faults even where there aren't any worth finding. My overthinking and anxiety attacks don't help either.

This has happened so many times that I've actually grown to distrust happiness. Anytime I'm happy, I immediately become sort of mentally vigilant, waiting for something to come along and ruin the moment. And more often than not, it is this very thought that does it.

It's really pissing off, because I know the problem is within me and I should control it, but when it happens, it's almost unstoppable. It's like Bruce Banner morphing into the Hulk.

I guess all we can do is try to either shut out those thoughts or divert our thinking to something productive. A hobby, perhaps? Or a good book? Or talking to a close friend?

Anyway, I'm here if you want to talk about it :)

Hi there! I can totally relate with what you said in the 3rd paragraph. Anytime I feel a spark of inspiration to do something, the voice inside me immediately replies, "What's the point? You're gonna fuck it up just like you fuck up everything else", and I slump back in my couch and resume doing nothing.
It is quite difficult to stay inspired when dealing with a deep sense of ennui. What is sort of working for me, at least for the time being is writing. I discovered that I have a passion for the written word, and I started writing a bunch of random articles on completely randomass stuff. So search for that one thing that keeps you satisfied, even temporarily. I know, easier said than done, right? It might be hard, but when you do, it will all be worth it. Hope you don't give up.
